# Angrove

> Angrove is a free, private study app for iPhone for the rigorous study of philosophy, history, and theology. Its language model, Google's Gemma 4 E4B, runs on the iPhone, so questions are not sent to a model server, and answers work offline once the model is downloaded. Answers are grounded in a Library of 37 primary works (51,836 passages) and cite the passages they draw on. Saved personal data is encrypted on the device.

Angrove is in public beta on iPhone through TestFlight; an App Store release is next. Angrove for Mac is planned for December 15, 2026. It needs no account. It is built by Ryan Baltodano and published by Sine Viridian.

Answers can be wrong, so the app keeps every cited source one tap away. Angrove is a tool for private study and reflection, not a substitute for professional counseling, spiritual direction, or clergy.

## Product

- [Home](https://angrove.app/): what Angrove is, its three commitments (privacy, grounded answers, personalization), the Insight Tree, and the Library
- [FAQ](https://angrove.app/faq.html): release, cost, which iPhones, data and encryption, the model, answer speed, and limits
- [User Guide](https://angrove.app/guide.html): asking questions, Insights, the Insight Tree, Midpoints, Study in 3D, Model Tasks, and privacy settings
- [Angrove for Mac](https://angrove.app/mac.html): Boards, a conversation beside its Insight Tree, and a choice of on-device models
- [Privacy Policy](https://angrove.app/privacy.html): what stays on the phone and the few cases where data leaves it

## Engineering

- [Case Studies](https://angrove.app/case-study.html): architecture, key decisions, and evidence for on-device inference, local retrieval, and encrypted storage
- [Development Notes](https://angrove.app/blog/): dated experiments and measurements
